mechanism_narrative: The observed sustained decline in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a persistent negative trend in discretionary spending and activity, which is likely to continue into the next four weeks as underlying conditions remain unchanged.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, following a sharp decline, suggests a renewed return to office work. If this rebound is sustained or strengthened, it will drive increased weekday footfall to retail and recreation establishments over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES maintains above -25% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining above -25% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in WORKPLACES mobility signifies a shift from home-centric activities to out-of-home work and associated errands. This behavioral change will positively impact retail and recreation over the short term (next two weeks).
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the average of the last 14 days, despite RESIDENTIAL decreasing and WORKPLACES increasing in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of TRANSIT mobility at t-0w after a sharp decline suggests that public transport usage is bottoming out or slightly recovering, potentially due to easing of restrictions or increased confidence, which will encourage more movement to retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is between -5 and +5 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if TRANSIT mobility stabilizes within the specified range.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently low PARKS mobility indicates a lack of outdoor leisure activity. In the absence of other positive drivers, this suggests a general reluctance for discretionary out-of-home activities, thus negatively impacting retail and recreation over the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -20% change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than the average of the last 7 days, while PARKS mobility remains below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, following a period of high essential spending, could indicate a shift in consumer priorities or a reduction in panic buying. This shift would potentially free up discretionary spending for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the average of the last 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM falling by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, coupled with a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, represents a strong return to pre-pandemic commuting and work patterns. This coordinated shift will directly translate to increased foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite a simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates that a significant portion of the population continues to stay home, limiting opportunities for out-of-home discretionary spending and thus suppressing retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 15% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even though RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 15% for two consecutive weeks.
